worktree: feat/combat-s1-pursuit @f0fc7ed (rev2: _pursuit_carry cross-event accumulator + hard erase on team death)
finding: rev2 accumulator (_pursuit_carry, keyed by loser_id, persists across pursuit events) is structurally correct and modeled on the working _cas_carry pattern (which DID fix the earlier annihilation zero-bleed bug). BUT: _cas_carry accumulates across many ROUNDS *within a single combat* (guaranteed repeat contributions to the same team_id before the encounter ends), whereas _pursuit_carry only gets ONE contribution per combat (pursuit fires once, at combat end) and only accumulates further if the SAME team_id is pursued again in a SEPARATE future combat. Across 218 combats / 18 seeds, all 14 pursuit events hit 14 distinct loser teams (or at minimum, no team_id was pursued a second time before the carry could cross 1.0) -- so the accumulator never had a second contribution to sum with the first, and output is byte-identical to the pre-rev2 (broken int()-truncation) run. This is not a failed de-patch -- the carry logic is sound -- it's a structural mismatch: the _cas_carry pattern relies on within-encounter round repetition to accumulate; pursuit has no equivalent repetition structure at organic scale.
implication_not_judged_by_measurer: For pursuit's cruelty/greed personalization to ever manifest in organic play, either (a) accept it as effectively a rare/dormant mechanism that only fires when the same team is unlucky enough to be pursued in back-to-back separate encounters (may never happen at typical world scale), or (b) change the accumulation unit -- e.g. carry across a team's entire lifetime is already what's implemented, so the real lever is increasing PURSUIT_RATE or lowering the reachability gate so single-event fractional loss crosses 1.0 more often, which reopens the 'personalization vs indiscriminate inflation' tradeoff the original spec was trying to avoid. Systems/blueprint call, not measured here.
